candidates.summary: The pulse says the newest activity event 'just joined', but the event has no height, and the realm keeps the seed's 'listed' events indefinitely, so the store shows stale events as news
candidates.failure_scenario: seed.gno's init upserts 12 listings at deploy, and each one tracks a 'listed' event. The activity ring (pulse.gno) has no expiry, and api/v1/home serves events as kind/slug/stars with no height. A year after deploy, with no new event, api/v1/home still serves [{"kind":"listed","slug":"valopers"},...], and gnoweb draws the pulse line 'Block 6307200 · <n>s ago · Valopers just joined'. Valopers joined at deploy. The same holds for any listing on an idle store. gnoweb has no field to tell the event's age, so the error is invisible to it.

candidates.summary: shortPath keeps only 4 data and 4 checksum characters of an address namespace, so a 40-bit vanity grind gives a look-alike namespace with the same short path, against the comment's 'never hidden by truncation'
candidates.failure_scenario: TruncMiddle(ns, 6, 4) shows 'g1', the first 4 data characters and the last 4 checksum characters ('g17zyd…9cxg/poll', store_test.go:332). At 5 bits per character that is 40 bits, about 1.1e12 key generations, which a GPU vanity search covers in minutes. An attacker grinds an address whose short path equals another anonymous app's, and their card's path line reads the same. Only the hover title shows the full path. Both cards carry the Community mark and titles stay unique, so the loss is the path line as an identifier.
